docs.title: Inertial Navigation Simulation & GUI
docs.text:
ins_sim is an open-source 6-DOF, WGS-84 strapdown INS Monte Carlo simulator with a desktop GUI. It generates a truth flight trajectory, derives the gyro and accelerometer outputs a perfect IMU would produce along it, corrupts them with a navigation-grade IMU error model, and runs a strapdown mechanization to recover position, velocity, and attitude. A Monte Carlo ensemble over independent noise realizations characterizes how navigation error grows over time for a given IMU grade.

Download the app View on GitHub

docs.title: Core features
docs.text:
• Truth trajectory generation from YAML mission profiles — waypoint legs, speed ramps, climbs, and turns, specified in conventional aviation units and converted to strict SI internally.
  • Navigation-grade IMU error model: angular/velocity random walk, Gauss-Markov bias drift, turn-on bias repeatability, scale-factor and misalignment errors, and initial-alignment errors, parameterized by a YAML datasheet spec.
  • Rotating-Earth strapdown mechanization: Earth rate, transport rate, WGS-84 radii of curvature, and Somigliana normal gravity evaluated at the current latitude/altitude every step — not a flat-Earth approximation.
  • Vertical channel physics: a third-order baro-damped loop by default, or free-inertial mode to observe the channel's inherent instability.
  • Monte Carlo evaluation: ensembles of independent noise realizations with CEP, per-axis error bands, and percentile statistics.
  • Interactive visualizations — every tab is a plotly page rendered in-app: CEP growth with a percentile table, attitude/velocity/position 3σ bands, a 3D trajectory with a 95th percentile error tube, and a ground-track map.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Data flows from truth generation, through noise injection, into the strapdown navigator, and is summarized by the Monte Carlo / evaluation layer:

flowchart TD
    CFG["Config (YAML)<br/>trajectory + IMU spec"]
    TRUTH["Truth generation<br/>trajectory/kinematics.py"]
    SENSOR["Noise addition<br/>sensors/imu.py"]
    NAV["Strapdown mechanization<br/>navigation/strapdown.py"]
    EVAL["Monte Carlo + plots<br/>evaluation/"]
    EARTH(["Earth model<br/>core/earth_model.py"])

    CFG --> TRUTH
    TRUTH -->|"true ω, specific force"| SENSOR
    SENSOR -->|"measured ω, f (+ noise)"| NAV
    NAV -->|"pos, vel, attitude"| EVAL
    EARTH -.->|"ω_ie, ω_en, g, R_N/R_E"| TRUTH
    EARTH -.-> NAV

docs.title: Conventions in brief
docs.text:
• Frames: local-level North-East-Down navigation frame (n) and a vehicle-fixed body frame (b: x forward, y right, z down).
  • Attitude: scalar-last quaternion [x, y, z, w] representing the body-to-NED rotation, per the scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation convention.
  • Units: strict SI inside the simulation core; YAML configs use conventional datasheet/aviation units (deg, kt, ft, °/hr, µg) and are converted at load time.

docs.title: Download & Install
docs.text:
Prebuilt portable bundles for Windows and Linux (x86-64 and ARM64) are attached to every GitHub Release. No Python installation is required — download, extract, and run.

Download for Windows Download for Linux

On the release page, grab the asset for your platform:

Platform Asset Run Windows (64-bit) ins_sim-vX.Y.Z-windows-x86_64.zip extract, run ins_sim.exe Linux (x86-64) ins_sim-vX.Y.Z-linux-x86_64.tar.gz extract, run ins_sim Linux (ARM64) ins_sim-vX.Y.Z-linux-aarch64.tar.gz extract, run ins_sim

Which Linux asset?

Run uname -m on the target machine: x86_64 → use the x86-64 asset; aarch64 → use the ARM64 asset. The ARM64 bundle covers Raspberry Pi 4/5 running the 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS and other ARM64/aarch64 Linux. 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS (armv7l) is not covered by a prebuilt bundle — see Raspberry Pi (32-bit) below.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
1. Download the .zip asset and extract it anywhere (no installer).
  2. Open the extracted ins_sim folder and run ins_sim.exe.

Windows SmartScreen

The binaries are not code-signed, so the first launch may show "Windows protected your PC". Click More info → Run anyway. Keep ins_sim.exe inside its folder — it needs the bundled libraries beside it.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
Pick the asset matching your CPU (uname -m) — x86_64 or aarch64:

# Intel/AMD 64-bit
tar xzf ins_sim-vX.Y.Z-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
./ins_sim/ins_sim

# ARM64 (aarch64)
tar xzf ins_sim-vX.Y.Z-linux-aarch64.tar.gz
./ins_sim/ins_sim

Runtime requirements

Bundles are built on Ubuntu 24.04, so a similarly recent glibc is required. Minimal installations may also need the Qt WebEngine system libraries:

sudo apt-get install libegl1 libgl1 libxkbcommon0 libnss3 libasound2t64

docs.title: Raspberry Pi
docs.text:
The ARM64 bundle (ins_sim-vX.Y.Z-linux-aarch64.tar.gz) is the one for a Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 — but only when it is running the 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS. Confirm first:

uname -m        # aarch64  → use the ARM64 bundle
                # armv7l   → 32-bit OS, see below

docs.title: Raspberry Pi (32-bit)
docs.text:
There is no prebuilt bundle for 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS (armv7l/armhf), and the desktop GUI cannot be installed there either — PySide6 publishes no 32-bit ARM wheels, so pip install ".[gui]" will not resolve. Two options, best first:

  1. Reflash to the 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS (the Pi 4/5 support it) and use the aarch64 bundle above, or run the GUI from source.

  2. Stay on 32-bit and run the headless CLI from source — it needs only numpy/scipy/pyyaml/matplotlib/plotly, no Qt:

    git clone https://github.com/jorgieo/ins_sim.git
cd ins_sim
pip install -e .          # base install, NOT ".[gui]"
python main.py            # writes an interactive maps/trajectory_map.html

    This produces the matplotlib summary figure and a standalone interactive ground-track map (open maps/trajectory_map.html in a browser) without the desktop front end. See the CLI options with python main.py --help.

docs.title: Internet access
docs.text: The application runs fully offline with one exception: the Map tab loads OpenStreetMap basemap tiles from the network. Every other visualization works without a connection.

docs.title: Run from source
docs.text:
Prefer a Python environment? Clone the repository and launch the GUI directly:

git clone https://github.com/jorgieo/ins_sim.git
cd ins_sim
pip install ".[gui]"
python -m ins_sim.gui

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: This guide walks through operating the desktop app, interpreting each visualization, and authoring your own mission and IMU configuration files.

docs.title: Running your first simulation
docs.text:
1. Select a trajectory. The Trajectory list shows the mission YAMLs in the trajectories folder next to the app: the app's own folder for the downloaded bundle, or the current working directory when run from source. On first launch the folder is created and seeded with the packaged bqn_departure.yaml. Files you add or edit there appear the next time you open the list, and your edits are never overwritten. Browse… opens the same folder and accepts any mission file with a top-level phases list. If that location is not writable, the app uses ~/ins_sim/trajectories instead.
  2. Select an IMU spec. Same pattern, with the imu_specs folder and the packaged navigation-grade imu_spec.yaml. Files must have top-level gyro and accel sections.
  3. Set the ensemble size. Monte Carlo iterations (default 50) trades statistical confidence against run time — ensemble statistics converge as \(1/\sqrt{N}\), so quadrupling the trials halves the noise on the percentile curves.
  4. Set the time step. Time step (dt) (default 0.1 s) is the truth and integration sample interval. 0.1 s is the reference setting; 0.5–1.0 s runs much faster and is fine for quick looks at long-duration error growth.
  5. Choose the vertical channel. Baro altitude aiding (checked by default) runs the third-order baro-damped vertical loop. Uncheck it to see the free-inertial vertical channel diverge — the instability is real physics, not a bug (see Theory & Math).
  6. Pick visualizations. Each checked box becomes one tab after the run.
  7. Run. The simulation executes on a background thread — the log pane streams progress (per-trial completion, timing, final 95th-percentile error) and the progress bar tracks the ensemble. The UI stays responsive throughout; controls re-enable when the run finishes.

docs.title: Reading the results
docs.text:
Every tab is an interactive plotly page — hover for values, drag to zoom, double-click to reset.

CEP (Circular Error Probable) — every trial's horizontal error in nautical miles against decimal hours, with the ensemble CEP drift-rate fit (fitted to the pointwise 50th percentile over the first hour). Below the plot, a table lists the 50th and 95th percentile error at each whole hour.

Attitude / Velocity / Position Errors — per-axis ensemble mean error with ±3σ bands, where σ is the sample standard deviation across trials. All three are resolved along the local North, East and Down axes at the true position, and every error is the estimate minus the truth (see Notation & conventions):

  • Attitude shows the small rotation between the estimated and the true attitude: the North and East tilts, and the heading error (the rotation about Down), in degrees.
  • Velocity and Position show the North, East and Down components. The position error is the latitude, longitude and height error converted to metres.

With baro aiding on, the Down channels stay bounded while North/East grow with the classic INS error signature; with aiding off, watch the Down channels run away.

3D Trajectory — the truth track (black), every trial's estimated track (steel blue), and the crimson swept tube of the 95th-percentile radial error.

Ground Track Map — the mission over OpenStreetMap tiles with the 95th-percentile horizontal-error envelope drawn perpendicular to the track and 5-minute markers along the truth path. The basemap tiles are the only part of the app that needs an internet connection.

docs.title: Writing mission profiles
docs.text:
A mission YAML has three top-level sections — departure, simulation_time, and phases. All angles are degrees, altitudes feet, speeds knots (or Mach); everything is converted to SI internally.

name: My Mission

departure:
  lat_deg:  18.4949        # start latitude
  lon_deg: -67.1294        # start longitude
  alt_ft:   237.0          # field elevation (MSL)
  nav_bank_angle_deg: 25.0 # bank angle used for inter-waypoint turns

simulation_time:
  dt_s: 0.1                # sample rate hint (GUI/CLI dt overrides it)

phases:
  - type: ground_roll
    ...

Phases execute in order; each starts from the state the previous one left (position, speed, heading, altitude).

Phase type Keys Behavior ground_roll heading_deg, run_length_m, speed_final_kt Accelerates along the runway heading over the given ground run. takeoff heading_deg, pitch_deg, speed_kt, duration_s Rotates and climbs out at the given pitch and speed. climb pitch_deg, speed_kt, to_altitude_ft Climbs at constant pitch/speed until reaching the target altitude. waypoint lat_deg, lon_deg, alt_ft, speed_kt (optional), loiter (optional) Flies a great-circle-style leg to the fix, turning at the departure-block bank angle. If speed_kt is omitted the leg inherits the current speed — e.g. a sprint leg flown at the Mach set by a preceding speed_ramp. speed_ramp speed_end_kt or speed_end_mach, duration_s Linear acceleration/deceleration to the target speed. speed_end_mach converts via the ISA sound speed at the current altitude.

The optional loiter block on a waypoint flies constant-bank circles on arrival:

loiter:
  n_turns:        5
  bank_angle_deg: 30.0
  direction:      right    # or left; default right

docs.title: Writing IMU specifications
docs.text:
An IMU YAML has gyro, accel, and optional alignment sections, all in conventional datasheet units; load_imu_spec converts to SI at load time.

name: Navigation-Grade RLG INS

gyro:
  arw_deg_per_rt_hr:        0.002   # Angular Random Walk [°/√hr]
  bias_instab_deg_per_hr:   0.01    # Bias instability, datasheet value [°/hr]
  bias_tau_s:               3600.0  # GM correlation time [s]
  repeatability_deg_per_hr: 0.01    # Turn-on bias repeatability 1σ [°/hr]
  scale_factor_ppm:         5.0     # Scale-factor error 1σ per axis [ppm]
  misalignment_urad:        50.0    # Axis misalignment 1σ per element [µrad]

accel:
  vrw_m_per_s_per_rt_hr:    0.005   # Velocity Random Walk [m/s/√hr]
  bias_instab_ug:           5.0     # Bias instability, datasheet value [µg]
  bias_tau_s:               3600.0  # GM correlation time [s]
  repeatability_ug:         25.0    # Turn-on bias repeatability 1σ [µg]
  scale_factor_ppm:         100.0   # Scale-factor error 1σ per axis [ppm]
  misalignment_urad:        50.0    # Axis misalignment 1σ per element [µrad]

alignment:
  tilt_std_deg:    0.0015   # initial N/E tilt error 1σ [°]
  heading_std_deg: 0.04     # initial azimuth error 1σ [°]
Key Physical meaning arw_deg_per_rt_hr / vrw_m_per_s_per_rt_hr White-noise density. Integrated angle (velocity) uncertainty grows as ARW·√t (VRW·√t). bias_instab_* + bias_tau_s Bias instability as quoted on the datasheet (the floor of the Allan deviation), and the correlation time of the first-order Gauss-Markov process that models it. ins_sim sets the process spread so that its Allan deviation peaks at the datasheet value; see Validation. repeatability_* Turn-on bias: a constant offset drawn once per trial. scale_factor_ppm Per-axis multiplicative error, drawn once per trial. misalignment_urad Sensor-triad axis misalignment, six independent small angles drawn once per trial. alignment: block Residual error of a stationary gyrocompass alignment, applied to the initial attitude of each trial. Physically, tilt ≈ accel repeatability / g and heading ≈ east-gyro repeatability / (Ωie cos φ) — the packaged 0.04° corresponds to 0.01 °/hr at ≈18.5° N.

scale_factor_ppm, misalignment_urad, and the alignment block are optional and default to zero (exact passthrough), so minimal diagnostic specs stay valid.

docs.title: Scripted workflows
docs.text:
The GUI and CLI drive the same engine. Headless run with the bundled defaults, or any custom files:

python main.py --config path/to/mission.yaml --imu-spec path/to/imu.yaml \
               --trials 100 --dt 0.1 --seed 7

Or call the pipeline directly from Python:

from ins_sim.trajectory.kinematics import build_trajectory
from ins_sim.sensors.imu import load_imu_spec
from ins_sim.evaluation.monte_carlo import run_monte_carlo, percentile_envelope

truth, v_sprint, R_turn = build_trajectory("mission.yaml", tau_i=0.1)
spec = load_imu_spec("imu_spec.yaml")

mc = run_monte_carlo(truth, spec, n_trials=100, seed=7, baro_aiding=True)
r95 = percentile_envelope(mc.est_r_lb_l, truth.r_lb_l, q=95)

Python names follow the symbols on the Notation & conventions page: for example, truth.r_lb_l is the true position relative to the start point, and mc.est_r_lb_l holds every trial's estimate of it.

The documentation figures on this site are produced by exactly this pipeline — see tools/generate_doc_plots.py in the repository.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Terms and abbreviations used across these pages. Hover over any of them elsewhere in the docs to see the same definition as a tooltip. Symbols (such as \(\wvec{ib}{b}\) or \(R_N\)) are defined on the Notation & conventions page.

ARW Angle random walk: gyro white noise. Integrated angle uncertainty grows as ARW·√t; datasheets quote it in °/√h. CEP Circular error probable: the radius of the circle, centred on the true position, that contains 50% of horizontal position errors. ECEF Earth-centred, Earth-fixed frame (e): rotates with the Earth. ECI Earth-centred inertial frame (i): does not rotate with the Earth. GM First-order Gauss–Markov process: exponentially correlated random noise with a steady-state standard deviation and a correlation time. GNSS Global navigation satellite system (GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou). IMU Inertial measurement unit: three gyros and three accelerometers on orthogonal axes. INS Inertial navigation system: an IMU plus the navigation equations that turn its outputs into position, velocity and attitude. ISA International Standard Atmosphere: the reference profile of temperature and pressure with altitude. MEMS Micro-electro-mechanical systems: low-cost silicon inertial sensors. MSL Mean sea level. NED North-East-Down: the local navigation frame (n) used throughout ins_sim. QNH The altimeter pressure setting that makes a barometric altimeter read field elevation on the ground. RLG Ring laser gyroscope: an optical gyro technology used in navigation-grade INS. VRW Velocity random walk: accelerometer white noise. Integrated velocity uncertainty grows as VRW·√t; datasheets quote it in m/s/√h. WGS-84 World Geodetic System 1984: the reference ellipsoid, Earth rotation rate and gravity model used by ins_sim.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
The simulator is a small Python package; the GUI and the command-line tool are thin layers on top of it. Each page below is generated from the docstrings in the source code.

Physics quantities are named after their symbols on the Notation & conventions page. For example, v_eb_n is \(\vvec{eb}{n}\), the velocity of the body relative to the Earth resolved in NED, and C_b_n is \(\Cmat{b}{n}\), the body-to-NED attitude. Prefixes mark the role of a value: meas_ for a sensor measurement, est_ for a navigation estimate, delta_ for an error.

Page What it covers Start with Earth model WGS-84 radii of curvature, Earth rate, transport rate, gravity normal_gravity, wgs84_radii Trajectory The truth trajectory from a mission YAML, and the ideal IMU outputs along it build_trajectory, TruthTrajectory Sensors The IMU error model load_imu_spec, generate_imu_samples Navigation The strapdown mechanization strapdown_navgrade Evaluation Monte Carlo runs and the navigation-error definitions run_monte_carlo, position_error Configuration Paths to the packaged default YAML files default_trajectory_path

docs.title: A complete run
docs.text:
This script runs ten Monte Carlo trials on the packaged mission and prints the 95th-percentile position error after one hour. It is the same file the test suite runs, so it stays in step with the code.

"""Monte Carlo run on the packaged mission: the 95th-percentile position error."""

import numpy as np

from ins_sim.config import default_imu_spec_path, default_trajectory_path
from ins_sim.evaluation.errors import position_error
from ins_sim.evaluation.monte_carlo import percentile_envelope, run_monte_carlo
from ins_sim.sensors.imu import load_imu_spec
from ins_sim.trajectory.kinematics import build_trajectory

# Truth trajectory at 1 s steps (tau_i) and the navigation-grade IMU spec.
truth, _, _ = build_trajectory(str(default_trajectory_path()), tau_i=1.0)
spec = load_imu_spec(str(default_imu_spec_path()))

# Ten independent trials of the noisy IMU and the strapdown navigator.
mc = run_monte_carlo(truth, spec, n_trials=10, seed=7)

# Position error (estimate minus truth) in metres along North, East, Down.
delta_r_eb_n = position_error(mc.est_L_b, mc.est_lambda_b, mc.est_h_b,
                              truth.L_b, truth.lambda_b, truth.h_b)
r95 = percentile_envelope(delta_r_eb_n, q=95)

one_hour = np.searchsorted(truth.t, 3600.0)
print(f"{truth.t[-1] / 60:.0f} min of flight, {mc.est_L_b.shape[0]} trials")
print(f"95th-percentile position error after 1 h: {r95[one_hour]:.0f} m")

docs.title: Earth model
docs.text: The WGS-84 ellipsoid: radii of curvature, Earth rotation rate, transport rate and gravity. Every function accepts a scalar or an array of samples.

docs.title: ins_sim.core.earth_model
docs.text:
WGS-84 Earth model.

Frames: ECI inertial (i), ECEF Earth-fixed (e), NED navigation (n), body (b). Position is curvilinear: geodetic latitude L_b, longitude lambda_b and geodetic height h_b. Velocity v_eb^n is resolved in NED. Gravity: Somigliana normal gravity + free-air height correction, with the local gravity vector g_b^n = [0, 0, +g(L_b, h_b)] (Down positive).

Symbols follow Groves (2013); see Notation & conventions.

docs.title: Radii
docs.text:
Bases: NamedTuple

Radii of curvature of the WGS-84 ellipsoid at a given latitude.

Attributes:

  • R_N (float | ndarray) –

    Meridian radius of curvature [m], which governs north-south motion: dL_b/dt = v_N / (R_N + h_b).

  • R_E (float | ndarray) –

    Transverse (prime-vertical) radius of curvature [m], which governs east-west motion: dlambda_b/dt = v_E / ((R_E + h_b)·cos L_b).

docs.title: wgs84_radii
docs.text:
wgs84_radii(L_b: ArrayLike) -> Radii

Computes the WGS-84 radii of curvature at a given geodetic latitude.

Parameters:

  • L_b (ArrayLike) –

    Geodetic latitude, scalar or shape (M,) [rad].

Returns:

  • Radii ( Radii ) –

    (R_N, R_E), the meridian and transverse radii of curvature [m], each with the shape of L_b. Unpacks positionally as R_N, R_E = wgs84_radii(L_b).

Examples:

At the equator the transverse radius is the semi-major axis and the meridian radius is at its smallest:

>>> from ins_sim.core.earth_model import wgs84_radii
>>> R_N, R_E = wgs84_radii(0.0)
>>> round(float(R_N)), round(float(R_E))
(6335439, 6378137)
Source code in ins_sim/core/earth_model.py 
def wgs84_radii(L_b: npt.ArrayLike) -> Radii:
    """Computes the WGS-84 radii of curvature at a given geodetic latitude.

    Args:
        L_b: Geodetic latitude, scalar or shape (M,) [rad].

    Returns:
        Radii: (R_N, R_E), the meridian and transverse radii of curvature
            [m], each with the shape of `L_b`. Unpacks positionally as
            ``R_N, R_E = wgs84_radii(L_b)``.

    Examples:
        At the equator the transverse radius is the semi-major axis and
        the meridian radius is at its smallest:

        >>> from ins_sim.core.earth_model import wgs84_radii
        >>> R_N, R_E = wgs84_radii(0.0)
        >>> round(float(R_N)), round(float(R_E))
        (6335439, 6378137)
    """
    # --8<-- [start:radii]
    sin2_L = np.sin(L_b) ** 2
    den    = np.sqrt(1.0 - WGS84_E2 * sin2_L)
    R_E    = WGS84_A / den                                    # transverse radius
    R_N    = WGS84_A * (1.0 - WGS84_E2) / (den ** 3)          # meridian radius
    # --8<-- [end:radii]
    return Radii(R_N, R_E)

earth_rate_n(L_b: ArrayLike) -> ndarray

Computes Earth's rotation rate resolved in the local NED frame.

def earth_rate_n(L_b: npt.ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray:
    """Computes Earth's rotation rate resolved in the local NED frame.

    Args:
        L_b: Geodetic latitude, scalar or shape (M,) [rad].

    Returns:
        numpy.ndarray: omega_ie^n, the Earth rotation rate vector [rad/s]
            resolved in NED. Shape (3,) for scalar `L_b`, shape (M, 3)
            for `L_b` of shape (M,).

    Examples:
        At 45° N the Earth's 15.04 °/h rotation splits equally between
        the North and (negative) Down axes:

        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from ins_sim.core.earth_model import earth_rate_n
        >>> omega_ie_n = earth_rate_n(np.deg2rad(45.0))
        >>> [round(float(x), 3) for x in np.rad2deg(omega_ie_n) * 3600]   # °/h
        [10.636, 0.0, -10.636]
    """
    L_b = np.asarray(L_b)
    zeros = np.zeros_like(L_b)
    # --8<-- [start:earth_rate]
    return np.stack(
        [WGS84_OMEGA * np.cos(L_b), zeros, -WGS84_OMEGA * np.sin(L_b)], axis=-1)

def transport_rate_n(v_eb_n: npt.ArrayLike, L_b: npt.ArrayLike,
                     h_b: npt.ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray:
    """Computes the transport rate of the NED frame relative to the Earth frame.

    The rotation rate of the local navigation frame caused by the
    vehicle's motion over the curved Earth, resolved in NED.

    Args:
        v_eb_n: Velocity of the body relative to the Earth, resolved in
            NED [v_N, v_E, v_D]. Shape (3,) or (M, 3) [m/s].
        L_b: Geodetic latitude, scalar or shape (M,) [rad].
        h_b: Geodetic height, scalar or shape (M,) [m].

    Returns:
        numpy.ndarray: omega_en^n, the transport rate vector [rad/s]
            resolved in NED. Shape (3,) for scalar inputs, shape (M, 3)
            for inputs of shape (M, 3)/(M,)/(M,).

    Examples:
        Flying due north at 250 m/s turns the local NED frame about its
        East axis (negative sign: the frame pitches nose-down to stay level):

        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from ins_sim.core.earth_model import transport_rate_n
        >>> omega_en_n = transport_rate_n([250.0, 0.0, 0.0], np.deg2rad(45.0), 4572.0)
        >>> [round(float(x), 3) for x in np.rad2deg(omega_en_n) * 3600]   # °/h
        [0.0, -8.09, 0.0]
    """
    v_eb_n = np.asarray(v_eb_n)
    L_b = np.asarray(L_b)
    h_b = np.asarray(h_b)
    R_N, R_E = wgs84_radii(L_b)
    v_N, v_E = v_eb_n[..., 0], v_eb_n[..., 1]
    # --8<-- [start:transport_rate]
    return np.stack([
         v_E / (R_E + h_b),
        -v_N / (R_N + h_b),
        -v_E * np.tan(L_b) / (R_E + h_b),
    ], axis=-1)

>>> from ins_sim.core.earth_model import normal_gravity
>>> round(float(normal_gravity(0.0, 0.0)), 7)       # equator, sea level

def normal_gravity(L_b: npt.ArrayLike, h_b: npt.ArrayLike) -> float | np.ndarray:
    """Computes normal gravity via the Somigliana formula with a free-air correction.

    Args:
        L_b: Geodetic latitude, scalar or shape (M,) [rad].
        h_b: Geodetic height, scalar or shape (M,) [m].

    Returns:
        float | numpy.ndarray: Local gravity magnitude g(L_b, h_b)
            [m/s²], with the shape of the inputs.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from ins_sim.core.earth_model import normal_gravity
        >>> round(float(normal_gravity(0.0, 0.0)), 7)       # equator, sea level
        9.7803253
        >>> round(float(normal_gravity(np.deg2rad(45.0), 10000.0)), 4)
        9.7754
    """
    g_e = 9.7803253359          # equatorial gravity
    k   = 1.93185265241e-3      # Somigliana ratio constant
    # --8<-- [start:gravity]
    sin2_L = np.sin(L_b) ** 2
    g0  = g_e * (1.0 + k * sin2_L) / np.sqrt(1.0 - WGS84_E2 * sin2_L)
    # Linear free-air correction: dg/dh ≈ −2g/R_0 near the surface
    return g0 * (1.0 - 2.0 * h_b / WGS84_A)

Monte Carlo evaluation: many independent runs of the noisy IMU and the navigator.

run_monte_carlo repeats the sensor-error draw and the strapdown navigation for a number of trials and collects every trial's estimates and attitude error. The spread across trials is the simulator's measure of navigation performance; percentile_envelope summarizes it as a position-error percentile over time.

docs.title: run_monte_carlo
docs.text:
run_monte_carlo(truth: TruthTrajectory, spec: IMUSpec, n_trials: int, seed: int = 0, progress_callback: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None, baro_aiding: bool = True) -> MonteCarloResult

Runs n_trials independent noisy-IMU strapdown realizations.

Each trial has its own random stream, spawned from seed, and each error source within a trial (initial alignment, IMU) draws from its own child stream. A trial's draws therefore do not depend on n_trials, and changing one error source's parameters leaves the other sources' realizations unchanged (common random numbers).

Parameters:

  • truth (TruthTrajectory) –

    Truth trajectory exposing t, tau_i, L_b, lambda_b, h_b, v_eb_n, C_b_n, omega_ib_b and f_ib_b.

  • spec (IMUSpec) –

    IMU error-parameter set used to generate noisy samples.

  • n_trials (int) –

    Number of independent Monte Carlo trials.

  • seed (int, default: 0 ) –

    Seed for the master random generator. Defaults to 0.

  • progress_callback (Callable[[int, int], None] | None, default: None ) –

    Optional callable invoked as progress_callback(n_done, n_trials) after each trial completes. Defaults to None (no reporting).

  • baro_aiding (bool, default: True ) –

    When True the strapdown runs with the baro-damped vertical channel (truth height as the baro measurement); when False the vertical channel is free-inertial and diverges. Defaults to True.

Returns:

  • MonteCarloResult ( MonteCarloResult ) –

    estimates and attitude errors for every trial.

Examples:

>>> from ins_sim.evaluation.monte_carlo import run_monte_carlo
>>> from ins_sim.sensors.imu import IMUSpec
>>> from ins_sim.trajectory.kinematics import TruthTrajectory
>>> from ins_sim.trajectory.spline import NEDSplinePath
>>> path = NEDSplinePath([[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [3000.0, 1000.0, -50.0]])
>>> truth = TruthTrajectory.from_spline(path, speed=150.0, tau_i=0.1)
>>> mc = run_monte_carlo(truth, IMUSpec(), n_trials=3, seed=1)
>>> mc.est_L_b.shape == (3, len(truth.t))
True
Source code in ins_sim/evaluation/monte_carlo.py 
def run_monte_carlo(truth: "TruthTrajectory", spec: IMUSpec,
                    n_trials: int, seed: int = 0,
                    progress_callback: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None,
                    baro_aiding: bool = True) -> MonteCarloResult:
    """Runs n_trials independent noisy-IMU strapdown realizations.

    Each trial has its own random stream, spawned from `seed`, and each
    error source within a trial (initial alignment, IMU) draws from its own
    child stream. A trial's draws therefore do not depend on `n_trials`, and
    changing one error source's parameters leaves the other sources'
    realizations unchanged (common random numbers).

    Args:
        truth: Truth trajectory exposing t, tau_i, L_b, lambda_b, h_b,
            v_eb_n, C_b_n, omega_ib_b and f_ib_b.
        spec: IMU error-parameter set used to generate noisy samples.
        n_trials: Number of independent Monte Carlo trials.
        seed: Seed for the master random generator. Defaults to 0.
        progress_callback: Optional callable invoked as
            progress_callback(n_done, n_trials) after each trial
            completes. Defaults to None (no reporting).
        baro_aiding: When True the strapdown runs with the baro-damped
            vertical channel (truth height as the baro measurement);
            when False the vertical channel is free-inertial and
            diverges. Defaults to True.

    Returns:
        MonteCarloResult: estimates and attitude errors for every trial.

    Examples:
        >>> from ins_sim.evaluation.monte_carlo import run_monte_carlo
        >>> from ins_sim.sensors.imu import IMUSpec
        >>> from ins_sim.trajectory.kinematics import TruthTrajectory
        >>> from ins_sim.trajectory.spline import NEDSplinePath
        >>> path = NEDSplinePath([[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [3000.0, 1000.0, -50.0]])
        >>> truth = TruthTrajectory.from_spline(path, speed=150.0, tau_i=0.1)
        >>> mc = run_monte_carlo(truth, IMUSpec(), n_trials=3, seed=1)
        >>> mc.est_L_b.shape == (3, len(truth.t))
        True
    """
    M = len(truth.t)
    est_r_lb_l     = np.zeros((n_trials, M, 3))
    est_euler_nb   = np.zeros((n_trials, M, 3))
    est_L_b        = np.zeros((n_trials, M))
    est_lambda_b   = np.zeros((n_trials, M))
    est_v_eb_n     = np.zeros((n_trials, M, 3))
    est_h_b        = np.zeros((n_trials, M))
    delta_psi_nb_n = np.zeros((n_trials, M, 3))

    trial_rngs = np.random.default_rng(seed).spawn(n_trials)
    C_b_n0 = truth.C_b_n[0]

    for i, trial_rng in enumerate(trial_rngs):
        rng_alignment, rng_imu = trial_rng.spawn(2)
        # Per-trial initial-alignment error delta_psi_nb^n: small NED tilts
        # plus an azimuth error, applied to the truth attitude (zero-mean
        # draws; exact truth initialization when the alignment stds are 0).
        delta_psi_nb_n0 = draw_initial_misalignment(spec, rng_alignment)
        est_C_b_n0 = Rot.from_rotvec(delta_psi_nb_n0) * C_b_n0
        init_state = NavState(
            truth.L_b[0], truth.lambda_b[0], truth.h_b[0],
            truth.v_eb_n[0].copy(),
            est_C_b_n0.as_quat(), # pyright: ignore[reportCallIssue]
        )
        meas_omega_ib_b, meas_f_ib_b = generate_imu_samples(truth, spec, rng_imu)
        nav = strapdown_navgrade(
            meas_omega_ib_b, meas_f_ib_b, init_state, truth.tau_i,
            meas_h_b=truth.h_b if baro_aiding else None)
        est_r_lb_l[i]   = nav.r_lb_l
        est_L_b[i]      = nav.L_b
        est_lambda_b[i] = nav.lambda_b
        est_h_b[i]      = nav.h_b
        est_v_eb_n[i]   = nav.v_eb_n
        est_C_b_n = Rot.from_quat(nav.q_b_n)
        delta_psi_nb_n[i] = attitude_error(est_C_b_n, truth.C_b_n)
        # as_euler('ZYX') → [psi, theta, phi]; reverse to [phi, theta, psi]
        est_euler_nb[i] = est_C_b_n.as_euler('ZYX')[:, ::-1]
        if progress_callback is not None:
            progress_callback(i + 1, n_trials)

    return MonteCarloResult(est_r_lb_l, est_euler_nb, est_L_b, est_lambda_b,
                            est_v_eb_n, est_h_b, delta_psi_nb_n)

def percentile_envelope(delta_r_eb_n: np.ndarray, q: float = 95) -> np.ndarray:
    """Computes the per-time-step q-th percentile of 3D position error magnitude.

    Args:
        delta_r_eb_n: Position error per trial (see
            `ins_sim.evaluation.errors.position_error`), shape
            (n_trials, M, 3) [m].
        q: Percentile to compute, in [0, 100]. Defaults to 95.

    Returns:
        numpy.ndarray: q-th percentile of the 3D error magnitude across
            trials at each time step, shape (M,) [m].

    Examples:
        Five trials whose errors are 1 to 5 m at every sample:

        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from ins_sim.evaluation.monte_carlo import percentile_envelope
        >>> delta_r = np.zeros((5, 2, 3))
        >>> delta_r[:, :, 0] = np.arange(1.0, 6.0)[:, None]

        [3.0, 3.0]
    """
    return np.percentile(np.linalg.norm(delta_r_eb_n, axis=2), q, axis=0)

Navigation error definitions, in Groves (2013) notation.

Every error is the estimate minus the truth. All three are resolved in the local NED axes at the true position, so attitude, velocity and position errors share one frame. They are also what the linearized error model (covariance analysis) propagates. The definitions are spelled out on Notation & conventions.

docs.text:
attitude_error(est_C_b_n: Rotation, C_b_n: Rotation) -> ndarray

Computes the attitude error delta_psi_nb^n.

The small rotation that takes the true attitude to the estimated one: C_b^n(estimated) = exp([delta_psi_nb^n ^]) · C_b^n(true), so delta_psi_nb^n is the rotation vector of C_b^n(estimated)·C_n^b(true). Its components are the North tilt, the East tilt and the Down (heading) error, resolved in NED.

Parameters:

  • est_C_b_n (Rotation) –

    Estimated body-to-NED attitude (scipy Rotation, single or stacked).

  • C_b_n (Rotation) –

    True body-to-NED attitude, with the same stacking.

Returns:

  • ndarray –

    numpy.ndarray: delta_psi_nb^n, shape (3,) or (M, 3) [rad].

Examples:

A 1 mrad heading error appears on the Down component:

>>> from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation
>>> from ins_sim.evaluation.errors import attitude_error
>>> C_b_n = Rotation.from_euler("ZYX", [30.0, 2.0, 5.0], degrees=True)
>>> est_C_b_n = Rotation.from_rotvec([0.0, 0.0, 1e-3]) * C_b_n
>>> [round(float(x), 6) for x in attitude_error(est_C_b_n, C_b_n)]
[0.0, 0.0, 0.001]

def attitude_error(est_C_b_n: Rotation, C_b_n: Rotation) -> np.ndarray:
    """Computes the attitude error delta_psi_nb^n.

    The small rotation that takes the true attitude to the estimated one:
    C_b^n(estimated) = exp([delta_psi_nb^n ^]) · C_b^n(true), so
    delta_psi_nb^n is the rotation vector of C_b^n(estimated)·C_n^b(true).
    Its components are the North tilt, the East tilt and the Down
    (heading) error, resolved in NED.

    Args:
        est_C_b_n: Estimated body-to-NED attitude (scipy Rotation, single
            or stacked).
        C_b_n: True body-to-NED attitude, with the same stacking.

    Returns:
        numpy.ndarray: delta_psi_nb^n, shape (3,) or (M, 3) [rad].

    Examples:
        A 1 mrad heading error appears on the Down component:

        >>> from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation
        >>> from ins_sim.evaluation.errors import attitude_error
        >>> C_b_n = Rotation.from_euler("ZYX", [30.0, 2.0, 5.0], degrees=True)
        >>> est_C_b_n = Rotation.from_rotvec([0.0, 0.0, 1e-3]) * C_b_n
        >>> [round(float(x), 6) for x in attitude_error(est_C_b_n, C_b_n)]
        [0.0, 0.0, 0.001]
    """
    return (est_C_b_n * C_b_n.inv()).as_rotvec()

docs.title: position_error
docs.text:
position_error(est_L_b: ArrayLike, est_lambda_b: ArrayLike, est_h_b: ArrayLike, L_b: ArrayLike, lambda_b: ArrayLike, h_b: ArrayLike) -> ndarray

Computes the position error delta_r_eb^n, resolved in NED at the true position.

The curvilinear errors (delta_L_b, delta_lambda_b, delta_h_b) are converted to metres along the local North, East and Down axes:

delta_r_eb^n = [(R_N + h_b)·delta_L_b,
                (R_E + h_b)·cos(L_b)·delta_lambda_b,
                −delta_h_b]

with the radii of curvature evaluated at the true latitude.

Parameters:

  • est_L_b (ArrayLike) –

    Estimated latitude [rad], shape (..., M).

  • est_lambda_b (ArrayLike) –

    Estimated longitude [rad], shape (..., M).

  • est_h_b (ArrayLike) –

    Estimated height [m], shape (..., M).

  • L_b (ArrayLike) –

    True latitude [rad], shape (M,), broadcast against the estimates.

  • lambda_b (ArrayLike) –

    True longitude [rad], shape (M,).

  • h_b (ArrayLike) –

    True height [m], shape (M,).

Returns:

  • ndarray –

    numpy.ndarray: delta_r_eb^n, shape (..., M, 3) [m].

Examples:

A 1 µrad latitude error at 45° N is about 6.4 m North; a height estimate 10 m too high is a −10 m Down error:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ins_sim.evaluation.errors import position_error
>>> L_b = np.deg2rad(45.0)
>>> delta_r = position_error(L_b + 1e-6, 0.0, 10.0, L_b, 0.0, 0.0)
>>> [round(float(x), 2) for x in delta_r]
[6.37, 0.0, -10.0]
Source code in ins_sim/evaluation/errors.py 
def position_error(est_L_b: npt.ArrayLike, est_lambda_b: npt.ArrayLike,
                   est_h_b: npt.ArrayLike, L_b: npt.ArrayLike,
                   lambda_b: npt.ArrayLike, h_b: npt.ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray:
    """Computes the position error delta_r_eb^n, resolved in NED at the true position.

    The curvilinear errors (delta_L_b, delta_lambda_b, delta_h_b) are
    converted to metres along the local North, East and Down axes:

        delta_r_eb^n = [(R_N + h_b)·delta_L_b,
                        (R_E + h_b)·cos(L_b)·delta_lambda_b,
                        −delta_h_b]

    with the radii of curvature evaluated at the true latitude.

    Args:
        est_L_b: Estimated latitude [rad], shape (..., M).
        est_lambda_b: Estimated longitude [rad], shape (..., M).
        est_h_b: Estimated height [m], shape (..., M).
        L_b: True latitude [rad], shape (M,), broadcast against the
            estimates.
        lambda_b: True longitude [rad], shape (M,).
        h_b: True height [m], shape (M,).

    Returns:
        numpy.ndarray: delta_r_eb^n, shape (..., M, 3) [m].

    Examples:
        A 1 µrad latitude error at 45° N is about 6.4 m North; a height
        estimate 10 m too high is a −10 m Down error:

        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from ins_sim.evaluation.errors import position_error
        >>> L_b = np.deg2rad(45.0)
        >>> delta_r = position_error(L_b + 1e-6, 0.0, 10.0, L_b, 0.0, 0.0)
        >>> [round(float(x), 2) for x in delta_r]
        [6.37, 0.0, -10.0]
    """
    L_b = np.asarray(L_b)
    h_b = np.asarray(h_b)
    delta_L_b = np.asarray(est_L_b) - L_b
    # Wrap the longitude difference to (−π, π] so a track crossing the
    # antimeridian does not show a spurious 2π jump.
    delta_lambda_b = np.mod(np.asarray(est_lambda_b) - lambda_b + np.pi, 2.0 * np.pi) - np.pi
    delta_h_b = np.asarray(est_h_b) - h_b
    R_N, R_E = wgs84_radii(L_b)
    return np.stack([
        (R_N + h_b) * delta_L_b,
        (R_E + h_b) * np.cos(L_b) * delta_lambda_b,
        -delta_h_b,
    ], axis=-1)

def plot_error_tube(ax: "Axes3D", r_lb_l: np.ndarray, r95: np.ndarray, color: str = "crimson",
                    alpha: float = 0.20, n_circle: int = 24) -> None:
    """Draws the swept-volume tube of the radial error envelope around the truth track.

    Args:
        ax: Matplotlib 3D axes to draw on.
        r_lb_l: Truth position relative to the start point (or a
            consistently scaled copy), shape (M, 3).
        r95: Radial error envelope at each time step, shape (M,), in
            the same units as r_lb_l.
        color: Surface color. Defaults to "crimson".
        alpha: Surface opacity. Defaults to 0.20.
        n_circle: Number of points approximating the tube's circular
            cross-section. Defaults to 24.

    Returns:
        None: Draws directly onto `ax`.
    """
    T = np.gradient(r_lb_l, axis=0)
    T = T / np.linalg.norm(T, axis=1, keepdims=True)

    seed = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
    if abs(T[0] @ seed) > 0.95:
        seed = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0])

    N1 = np.zeros_like(T); N2 = np.zeros_like(T)
    n  = seed - T[0] * (T[0] @ seed)
    N1[0] = n / np.linalg.norm(n)
    N2[0] = np.cross(T[0], N1[0])
    for k in range(1, len(T)):
        proj = N1[k-1] - T[k] * (T[k] @ N1[k-1])
        nn   = np.linalg.norm(proj)
        N1[k] = proj / nn if nn > 1e-10 else N1[k-1]
        N2[k] = np.cross(T[k], N1[k])

    th = np.linspace(0.0, 2*np.pi, n_circle)
    c, s = np.cos(th), np.sin(th)
    tube = (r_lb_l[:, None, :]
            + r95[:, None, None] * (c[None, :, None] * N1[:, None, :]
                                  + s[None, :, None] * N2[:, None, :]))

    X = tube[..., 1]      # East
    Y = tube[..., 0]      # North
    Z = -tube[..., 2]     # Up
    ax.plot_surface(X, Y, Z, color=color, alpha=alpha,
                    edgecolor='none', linewidth=0)

def build_summary_figure(truth: "TruthTrajectory", mc: "MonteCarloResult",
                         r95: np.ndarray) -> plt.Figure:
    """Builds the 2x3 Monte Carlo summary figure.

    Figure panels: 3D ground track with swept 95th-pct error tube,
    3D position-error envelope, CEP, and the three components of the
    attitude error delta_psi_nb^n. Does not call plt.show() -- the
    caller decides.

    Note:
        Applies sns.set_theme(...) as a side effect (global rcParams
        mutation), matching the original script's behavior.

    Args:
        truth: Truth trajectory exposing r_lb_l, t, L_b, lambda_b and h_b.
        mc: MonteCarloResult from run_monte_carlo.
        r95: 95th-percentile 3D position-error envelope, shape (M,) [m].

    Returns:
        matplotlib.figure.Figure: The assembled summary figure.
    """
    sns.set_theme(
        style='whitegrid',
        palette='deep',
        font_scale=1.05,
        rc={
            'figure.facecolor': '#f5f5f5',
            'axes.facecolor':   'white',
            'grid.color':       '#dddddd',
            'axes.edgecolor':   '#aaaaaa',
            'text.color':       '#111111',
            'axes.labelcolor':  '#111111',
            'xtick.color':      '#333333',
            'ytick.color':      '#333333',
        },
    )

    n_trials = len(mc.est_r_lb_l)
    P   = truth.r_lb_l
    t_m = truth.t / 60.0   # minutes for x-axis
    delta_r_eb_n = position_error(mc.est_L_b, mc.est_lambda_b, mc.est_h_b,
                                  truth.L_b, truth.lambda_b, truth.h_b)

    step = max(1, len(P) // 4000)
    fig  = plt.figure(figsize=(22, 12), layout='constrained')
    gs   = fig.add_gridspec(2, 3)

    ax  = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0], projection='3d')
    ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
    ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
    ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])   # North tilt
    ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])   # East tilt
    ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])   # Heading

    # ---- 3-D ground track + 95th-pct error tube ---------------------------
    # Isotropic km units (not the nm/kft mix used elsewhere) so the tube's
    # circular cross-section and tangent direction stay geometrically
    # correct: plot_error_tube offsets by a scalar radius (r95, in meters)
    # along normals derived from the track's own tangent, so all three axes
    # must share one linear scale factor.
    P_km = P / 1000.0
    r95_km = r95 / 1000.0
    ax.plot(P_km[::step, 1], P_km[::step, 0], -P_km[::step, 2],
            'k-', lw=1.5, label='Truth')
    for i in range(min(6, n_trials)):
        Q_km = mc.est_r_lb_l[i] / 1000.0
        ax.plot(Q_km[::step, 1], Q_km[::step, 0], -Q_km[::step, 2],
                '-', color='steelblue', alpha=0.35, lw=0.5)
    plot_error_tube(ax, P_km, r95_km)
    ax.set_xlabel('East (km)')
    ax.set_ylabel('North (km)')
    ax.set_zlabel('Up (km)')
    ax.set_title(f'{n_trials}-trial Monte Carlo')
    ax.legend(loc='upper left')

    # ---- 3-D position error vs time ---------------------------------------
    err_all = np.linalg.norm(delta_r_eb_n, axis=2)
    ax2.plot(t_m, err_all.T, color='steelblue', alpha=0.20, lw=0.5)
    ax2.plot(t_m, r95, color='crimson', lw=2.0, label='95th pct')
    ax2.fill_between(t_m, 0, r95, color='crimson', alpha=0.15)
    ax2.set_xlabel('Time (min)')
    ax2.set_ylabel('3-D position error (m)')
    ax2.set_title('Position error envelope')
    ax2.legend()

    # ---- CEP vs time + linear fit -----------------------------------------
    horiz_err = np.linalg.norm(delta_r_eb_n[:, :, :2], axis=2)
    cep = np.percentile(horiz_err, 50, axis=0)

    mask60 = t_m <= 60.0
    coeffs = np.polyfit(t_m[mask60], cep[mask60], 1)
    cep_fit = np.polyval(coeffs, t_m)

    ax3.plot(t_m, horiz_err.T, color='steelblue', alpha=0.15, lw=0.5)
    ax3.plot(t_m, cep, color='navy', lw=2.0, label='CEP (50th pct)')
    ax3.fill_between(t_m, 0, cep, color='steelblue', alpha=0.18)
    ax3.plot(t_m, cep_fit, '--', color='darkorange', lw=1.8,
             label=f'Linear fit  {coeffs[0]*0.032397408:.2f} NM/hr')
    ax3.axvline(60.0, color='gray', lw=0.8, linestyle=':')
    ax3.set_xlabel('Time (min)')
    ax3.set_ylabel('Horizontal error (m)')
    ax3.set_title('CEP along path')
    ax3.legend()

    # ---- Attitude error delta_psi_nb^n ------------------------------------
    delta_psi_deg = np.rad2deg(mc.delta_psi_nb_n)
    p95_abs = np.percentile(np.abs(delta_psi_deg), 95, axis=0)

    for ax_att, col, title in [
        (ax4, 0, 'North tilt error'),
        (ax5, 1, 'East tilt error'),
        (ax6, 2, 'Heading error'),
    ]:
        ax_att.plot(t_m, delta_psi_deg[:, :, col].T, color='steelblue',
                    alpha=0.20, lw=0.5)
        ax_att.fill_between(t_m, -p95_abs[:, col], p95_abs[:, col],
                            color='crimson', alpha=0.20,
                            label='95th pct |error|')
        ax_att.axhline(0.0, color='gray', lw=0.8)
        ax_att.set_xlabel('Time (min)')
        ax_att.set_ylabel(f'{title} (deg)')
        ax_att.set_title(title)
        ax_att.legend(fontsize=8)

    return fig

Strapdown inertial navigation in the local North-East-Down frame.

strapdown_navgrade integrates gyro and accelerometer outputs into attitude, velocity and curvilinear position on the rotating WGS-84 Earth, accounting for Earth rate, transport rate, Coriolis and normal gravity. An optional barometric height measurement stabilizes the vertical channel, which is unstable when the navigator runs on inertial sensors alone.

docs.title: strapdown_navgrade
docs.text:
strapdown_navgrade(meas_omega_ib_b: ndarray, meas_f_ib_b: ndarray, init_state: NavState | Sequence, tau_i: float, meas_h_b: ndarray | None = None, baro_tau: float = 100.0) -> NavSolution

Runs local-level (NED) strapdown integration with rotating-Earth corrections.

Each step (Groves notation):

  1. Evaluate omega_ie^n, omega_en^n and g(L_b, h_b) at the current state.
  2. Body rate relative to the navigation frame: omega_nb^b = omega_ib^b − C_n^b·(omega_ie^n + omega_en^n).
  3. Update C_b^n with the exact rotation-vector exponential of omega_nb^b·tau_i.
  4. Resolve specific force into NED: f_ib^n = C_b^n·f_ib^b.
  5. Velocity update, forward Euler: dv_eb^n/dt = f_ib^n − (2·omega_ie^n + omega_en^n) × v_eb^n + g_b^n.
  6. Curvilinear position update, forward Euler.

Parameters:

  • meas_omega_ib_b (ndarray) –

    Gyro output, angular rate of the body relative to inertial space resolved in body axes, shape (M, 3) [rad/s].

  • meas_f_ib_b (ndarray) –

    Accelerometer output, specific force resolved in body axes, shape (M, 3) [m/s²].

  • init_state (NavState | Sequence) –

    Initial state (L_b, lambda_b, h_b, v_eb_n, q_b_n): a NavState, or any sequence of those five values in that order.

  • tau_i (float) –

    Integration interval [s].

  • meas_h_b (ndarray | None, default: None ) –

    Optional barometric height measurement, shape (M,) [m]. When provided it drives a third-order baro-damped vertical channel: the INS-minus-baro height residual feeds proportional corrections into the height and vertical-velocity updates plus an integral state that absorbs steady vertical accelerometer error. This stabilises the inherently unstable vertical channel of a free-inertial navigator (the +√(2g/R) eigenvalue from the free-air gravity gradient). When None the vertical channel runs free-inertial and diverges accordingly. Defaults to None.

  • baro_tau (float, default: 100.0 ) –

    Time constant of the baro-damping loop [s]; the three gains place a triple pole at −1/baro_tau. Only used when meas_h_b is given. Defaults to 100.0.

Returns:

  • NavSolution ( NavSolution ) –

    (r_lb_l, L_b, lambda_b, h_b, v_eb_n, q_b_n) at every sample; unpacks positionally in that order.

Examples:

A level IMU at rest senses only Earth rate and gravity, and the navigator stays exactly at rest:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation
>>> from ins_sim.core.earth_model import earth_rate_n, normal_gravity
>>> from ins_sim.navigation.strapdown import NavState, strapdown_navgrade
>>> L_b = np.deg2rad(45.0)
>>> gyro = np.tile(earth_rate_n(L_b), (100, 1))
>>> accel = np.tile([0.0, 0.0, -normal_gravity(L_b, 0.0)], (100, 1))
>>> start = NavState(L_b, 0.0, 0.0, np.zeros(3), Rotation.identity().as_quat())
>>> nav = strapdown_navgrade(gyro, accel, start, tau_i=0.1)
>>> float(np.abs(nav.v_eb_n).max())
0.0

def strapdown_navgrade(meas_omega_ib_b: np.ndarray, meas_f_ib_b: np.ndarray,
                       init_state: NavState | Sequence, tau_i: float,
                       meas_h_b: np.ndarray | None = None,
                       baro_tau: float = 100.0) -> NavSolution:
    """Runs local-level (NED) strapdown integration with rotating-Earth corrections.

    Each step (Groves notation):

    1. Evaluate omega_ie^n, omega_en^n and g(L_b, h_b) at the current state.
    2. Body rate relative to the navigation frame:
       `omega_nb^b = omega_ib^b − C_n^b·(omega_ie^n + omega_en^n)`.
    3. Update C_b^n with the exact rotation-vector exponential of
       omega_nb^b·tau_i.
    4. Resolve specific force into NED: `f_ib^n = C_b^n·f_ib^b`.
    5. Velocity update, forward Euler:
       `dv_eb^n/dt = f_ib^n − (2·omega_ie^n + omega_en^n) × v_eb^n + g_b^n`.
    6. Curvilinear position update, forward Euler.

    Args:
        meas_omega_ib_b: Gyro output, angular rate of the body relative to
            inertial space resolved in body axes, shape (M, 3) [rad/s].
        meas_f_ib_b: Accelerometer output, specific force resolved in body
            axes, shape (M, 3) [m/s²].
        init_state: Initial state (L_b, lambda_b, h_b, v_eb_n, q_b_n): a
            NavState, or any sequence of those five values in that order.
        tau_i: Integration interval [s].
        meas_h_b: Optional barometric height measurement, shape (M,) [m].
            When provided it drives a third-order baro-damped vertical
            channel: the INS-minus-baro height residual feeds proportional
            corrections into the height and vertical-velocity updates plus
            an integral state that absorbs steady vertical accelerometer
            error. This stabilises the inherently unstable vertical channel
            of a free-inertial navigator (the +√(2g/R) eigenvalue from the
            free-air gravity gradient). When None the vertical channel runs
            free-inertial and diverges accordingly. Defaults to None.
        baro_tau: Time constant of the baro-damping loop [s]; the three
            gains place a triple pole at −1/baro_tau. Only used when
            meas_h_b is given. Defaults to 100.0.

    Returns:
        NavSolution: (r_lb_l, L_b, lambda_b, h_b, v_eb_n, q_b_n) at every
            sample; unpacks positionally in that order.

    Examples:
        A level IMU at rest senses only Earth rate and gravity, and the
        navigator stays exactly at rest:

        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation
        >>> from ins_sim.core.earth_model import earth_rate_n, normal_gravity
        >>> from ins_sim.navigation.strapdown import NavState, strapdown_navgrade
        >>> L_b = np.deg2rad(45.0)
        >>> gyro = np.tile(earth_rate_n(L_b), (100, 1))
        >>> accel = np.tile([0.0, 0.0, -normal_gravity(L_b, 0.0)], (100, 1))
        >>> start = NavState(L_b, 0.0, 0.0, np.zeros(3), Rotation.identity().as_quat())
        >>> nav = strapdown_navgrade(gyro, accel, start, tau_i=0.1)
        >>> float(np.abs(nav.v_eb_n).max())
        0.0
    """
    M = len(meas_omega_ib_b)
    L_b = np.zeros(M); lambda_b = np.zeros(M); h_b = np.zeros(M)
    v_eb_n = np.zeros((M, 3)); q_b_n = np.zeros((M, 4))
    r_lb_l = np.zeros((M, 3))          # for plotting against truth

    L_b[0], lambda_b[0], h_b[0], v_eb_n[0], q_b_n[0] = init_state
    C_b_n = Rot.from_quat(q_b_n[0])
    L_b0 = L_b[0]                      # reference for the local NED display
    h_b0 = h_b[0]
    R_N0, R_E0 = wgs84_radii(L_b0)     # loop-invariant: L_b0 never changes
    g_b_n = np.zeros(3)                # reused each iteration

    # --8<-- [start:baro_gains]
    # Third-order baro-damping gains: triple pole at -1/baro_tau for the
    # (height error, vertical-velocity error, accel-error integrator) loop.
    if meas_h_b is not None:
        K1 = 3.0 / baro_tau
        K2 = 3.0 / baro_tau ** 2
        K3 = 1.0 / baro_tau ** 3
        acc_corr = 0.0                 # integral state [m/s²], → -δa_D
    # --8<-- [end:baro_gains]

    for k in range(M - 1):
        # --8<-- [start:frame_rates]
        # --- 1. Local rotating-Earth quantities at step k --------------
        omega_ie_n = earth_rate_n(L_b[k])
        omega_en_n = transport_rate_n(v_eb_n[k], L_b[k], h_b[k])
        omega_in_n = omega_ie_n + omega_en_n                   # nav-frame rate
        g_b_n[2] = normal_gravity(L_b[k], h_b[k])
        # --8<-- [end:frame_rates]

        # --8<-- [start:body_rate]
        # --- 2. Body rate relative to the nav frame ------------------
        # The gyro saw omega_ib^b. Subtract the nav frame's own rotation
        # (resolved in body axes) to get what drives the b→n attitude update.
        C_n_b = C_b_n.inv()
        omega_nb_b = meas_omega_ib_b[k] - C_n_b.apply(omega_in_n)
        # --8<-- [end:body_rate]

        # --8<-- [start:attitude_update]
        # --- 3. Attitude update (exact rotation-vector exponential) ---
        dC = Rot.from_rotvec(omega_nb_b * tau_i)
        C_b_n_next = C_b_n * dC                                # right-mult: body increment
        q_b_n[k+1] = C_b_n_next.as_quat() # pyright: ignore[reportCallIssue]
        # --8<-- [end:attitude_update]

        # --8<-- [start:specific_force_transform]
        # --- 4. Specific force in NED (forward Euler — consistent with
        #        the truth IMU, which uses the same first-order scheme) ---
        f_ib_n = C_b_n.apply(meas_f_ib_b[k])
        # --8<-- [end:specific_force_transform]

        # --8<-- [start:velocity_update]
        # --- 5. Rotating-frame velocity update ------------------------
        coriolis = np.cross(2.0 * omega_ie_n + omega_en_n, v_eb_n[k])
        v_eb_n_dot = f_ib_n - coriolis + g_b_n
        # Baro damping: the height residual corrects vertical velocity
        # (K2) and updates the accel-error integrator (K3); a positive
        # residual (INS high) commands positive Down velocity.
        if meas_h_b is not None:
            baro_residual = h_b[k] - meas_h_b[k]
            v_eb_n_dot[2] += K2 * baro_residual + acc_corr
            acc_corr += K3 * baro_residual * tau_i
        v_eb_n[k+1] = v_eb_n[k] + v_eb_n_dot * tau_i
        # --8<-- [end:velocity_update]

        # --8<-- [start:position_update]
        # --- 6. Curvilinear position (forward Euler — matches truth) --
        R_N, R_E = wgs84_radii(L_b[k])
        L_b[k+1] = L_b[k] + (v_eb_n[k][0] / (R_N + h_b[k])) * tau_i
        lambda_b[k+1] = lambda_b[k] + (v_eb_n[k][1] /
                                       ((R_E + h_b[k]) * np.cos(L_b[k]))) * tau_i
        h_b[k+1] = h_b[k] - v_eb_n[k][2] * tau_i
        if meas_h_b is not None:
            h_b[k+1] -= K1 * baro_residual * tau_i
        # --8<-- [end:position_update]

        # Position relative to the start point (for plotting against
        # truth): linearized curvilinear-to-metres conversion using the
        # start-point radii R_N0, R_E0.
        r_lb_l[k+1, 0] = (L_b[k+1] - L_b0) * (R_N0 + h_b0)
        r_lb_l[k+1, 1] = (lambda_b[k+1] - lambda_b[0]) * (R_E0 + h_b0) * np.cos(L_b0)
        r_lb_l[k+1, 2] = -(h_b[k+1] - h_b0)

        C_b_n = C_b_n_next

    return NavSolution(r_lb_l, L_b, lambda_b, h_b, v_eb_n, q_b_n)

IMU error model: datasheet parameters and simulated gyro and accelerometer outputs.

An IMUSpec, usually loaded from YAML with load_imu_spec, sets the spread of each error term in the Groves (2013) sensor model:

meas_f_ib_b     = b_a + (I + M_a)·f_ib_b     + w_a
meas_omega_ib_b = b_g + (I + M_g)·omega_ib_b + w_g

generate_imu_samples draws one realization of these errors along a truth trajectory, and draw_initial_misalignment draws the initial alignment error. The terms are described on Notation & conventions.

IMUSpec(gyro_arw: float = 0.002 * pi / 180 / 60, gyro_bias_instability: float = 0.01 * pi / 180 / 3600, gyro_bias_tau: float = 3600.0, gyro_br_std: float = 0.01 * pi / 180 / 3600, gyro_sf_std: float = 0.0, gyro_ma_std: float = 0.0, accel_vrw: float = 0.005 / 60, accel_bias_instability: float = 5e-06 * 9.80665, accel_bias_tau: float = 3600.0, accel_br_std: float = 2.5e-05 * 9.80665, accel_sf_std: float = 0.0, accel_ma_std: float = 0.0, align_tilt_std: float = 0.0, align_heading_std: float = 0.0)

Navigation-grade IMU error parameters, as quoted on a sensor datasheet.

The defaults are typical of fielded navigation-grade systems, such as a ring-laser-gyro aircraft INS:

Parameter Gyro Accelerometer Random walk (ARW, VRW) 0.002 °/√h 0.005 m/s/√h Bias instability 0.01 °/h 5 µg Turn-on repeatability 0.01 °/h 25 µg

Every field is a datasheet parameter in SI units; each one sets the spread of a Groves (2013) error term (see the Notation & conventions page). Bias instability is the datasheet value, the floor of the sensor's Allan deviation. The in-run bias is simulated as a first-order Gauss-Markov process whose steady-state spread (gyro_gm_std, accel_gm_std) is chosen so that its Allan deviation peaks at exactly that value.

Attributes:

  • gyro_arw (float) –

    Gyro angular random walk, the density of the white noise w_g [rad/√s].

  • gyro_bias_instability (float) –

    Gyro bias instability from the datasheet, the floor of the Allan deviation [rad/s]. Sets the dynamic bias b_gd.

  • gyro_bias_tau (float) –

    Correlation time of the Gauss-Markov process that models the gyro bias instability [s].

  • gyro_br_std (float) –

    Gyro turn-on bias repeatability, the std dev of the static bias b_gs [rad/s].

  • gyro_sf_std (float) –

    Gyro scale-factor error std dev (diagonal of M_g), drawn once per run per axis [dimensionless, e.g. 5e-6 = 5 ppm].

  • gyro_ma_std (float) –

    Gyro axis-misalignment std dev (off-diagonal of M_g), drawn once per run per element [rad].

  • accel_vrw (float) –

    Accelerometer velocity random walk, the density of the white noise w_a [(m/s)/√s].

  • accel_bias_instability (float) –

    Accelerometer bias instability from the datasheet, the floor of the Allan deviation [m/s²]. Sets the dynamic bias b_ad.

  • accel_bias_tau (float) –

    Correlation time of the Gauss-Markov process that models the accelerometer bias instability [s].

  • accel_br_std (float) –

    Accelerometer turn-on bias repeatability, the std dev of the static bias b_as [m/s²].

  • accel_sf_std (float) –

    Accelerometer scale-factor error std dev (diagonal of M_a) [dimensionless].

  • accel_ma_std (float) –

    Accelerometer axis-misalignment std dev (off-diagonal of M_a) [rad].

  • align_tilt_std (float) –

    Initial-alignment tilt (N/E) error std dev [rad]. Physically ≈ accel repeatability / g.

  • align_heading_std (float) –

    Initial-alignment heading (azimuth) error std dev [rad]. Physically ≈ gyrocompass limit, gyro repeatability / (omega_ie·cos L_b).

Note

The multiplicative (scale factor, misalignment) and initial-alignment terms default to zero — they apply only when specified — so zero-noise diagnostic specs and legacy YAMLs keep their exact-passthrough behavior.

def load_imu_spec(yaml_path: str) -> IMUSpec:
    """Loads an IMUSpec from a YAML file expressed in datasheet units.

    Args:
        yaml_path: Path to a YAML file with `gyro` and `accel` sections
            in datasheet units (deg/√hr, deg/hr, µg, etc.).

    Returns:
        IMUSpec: Equivalent error-parameter set converted to SI units.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from ins_sim.config import default_imu_spec_path
        >>> from ins_sim.sensors.imu import load_imu_spec
        >>> spec = load_imu_spec(str(default_imu_spec_path()))
        >>> round(float(np.rad2deg(spec.gyro_arw) * 60), 4)   # back to °/√h
        0.002
    """
    with open(yaml_path) as fh:
        cfg = yaml.safe_load(fh)
    g = cfg["gyro"]
    a = cfg["accel"]
    al = cfg.get("alignment", {})
    DEG_HR = np.pi / 180 / 3600
    return IMUSpec(
        gyro_arw     = g["arw_deg_per_rt_hr"]          * np.pi / 180 / 60,
        gyro_bias_instability = g["bias_instab_deg_per_hr"]  * DEG_HR,
        gyro_bias_tau         = g["bias_tau_s"],
        gyro_br_std  = g["repeatability_deg_per_hr"]   * DEG_HR,
        gyro_sf_std  = g.get("scale_factor_ppm", 0.0)   * 1e-6,
        gyro_ma_std  = g.get("misalignment_urad", 0.0)  * 1e-6,
        accel_vrw    = a["vrw_m_per_s_per_rt_hr"]      / 60,
        accel_bias_instability = a["bias_instab_ug"]     * 1e-6 * 9.80665,
        accel_bias_tau         = a["bias_tau_s"],
        accel_br_std = a["repeatability_ug"]            * 1e-6 * 9.80665,
        accel_sf_std = a.get("scale_factor_ppm", 0.0)   * 1e-6,
        accel_ma_std = a.get("misalignment_urad", 0.0)  * 1e-6,
        align_tilt_std    = al.get("tilt_std_deg", 0.0)    * np.pi / 180,
        align_heading_std = al.get("heading_std_deg", 0.0) * np.pi / 180,
    )

                              rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:

    and a larger azimuth error about Down (limited by east-gyro bias

    exp([delta_psi_nb^n ^])·C_b^n(true).

docs.text:
generate_imu_samples(truth: TruthTrajectory, spec: IMUSpec, rng: Generator) -> IMUSamples

Generates noisy IMU samples from a truth trajectory and an error spec.

Per-axis IMU model (Groves notation):

meas_f_ib_b     = b_a + (I + M_a)·f_ib_b     + w_a
meas_omega_ib_b = b_g + (I + M_g)·omega_ib_b + w_g
  • M_a, M_g: scale factor (diagonal) and misalignment (off-diagonal), drawn once per run.
  • b_as, b_gs: static (turn-on) bias ~ N(0, σ_BR²), drawn once per run.
  • b_ad, b_gd: dynamic bias, a first-order Gauss-Markov process with correlation time τ and steady-state spread σ = B / GM_ALLAN_PEAK, so that its Allan deviation peaks at the datasheet bias instability B. Stationary from t = 0.
  • w_a, w_g: white noise, with σ = VRW/√tau_i or ARW/√tau_i per sample.

The gyro and accelerometer triads draw from separate random streams spawned from rng, so changing one triad's parameters leaves the other's error realization unchanged.

Parameters:

  • truth (TruthTrajectory) –

    Truth trajectory exposing t, tau_i, omega_ib_b (shape (M, 3) [rad/s]) and f_ib_b (shape (M, 3) [m/s²]).

  • spec (IMUSpec) –

    IMU error-parameter set.

  • rng (Generator) –

    Seeded NumPy random generator. Two child streams are spawned from it, one per sensor triad.

Returns:

  • IMUSamples ( IMUSamples ) –

    (meas_omega_ib_b, meas_f_ib_b), the noisy gyro and accelerometer outputs, each shape (M, 3).

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ins_sim.sensors.imu import IMUSpec, generate_imu_samples
>>> from ins_sim.trajectory.kinematics import TruthTrajectory
>>> from ins_sim.trajectory.spline import NEDSplinePath
>>> path = NEDSplinePath([[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [1000.0, 0.0, 0.0]])
>>> truth = TruthTrajectory.from_spline(path, speed=100.0, tau_i=0.1)
>>> imu = generate_imu_samples(truth, IMUSpec(), np.random.default_rng(1))
>>> imu.meas_omega_ib_b.shape == truth.omega_ib_b.shape
True

def generate_imu_samples(truth: "TruthTrajectory", spec: IMUSpec,
                         rng: np.random.Generator) -> IMUSamples:
    """Generates noisy IMU samples from a truth trajectory and an error spec.

    Per-axis IMU model (Groves notation):

        meas_f_ib_b     = b_a + (I + M_a)·f_ib_b     + w_a
        meas_omega_ib_b = b_g + (I + M_g)·omega_ib_b + w_g

    - M_a, M_g: scale factor (diagonal) and misalignment (off-diagonal),
      drawn once per run.
    - b_as, b_gs: static (turn-on) bias ~ N(0, σ_BR²), drawn once per run.
    - b_ad, b_gd: dynamic bias, a first-order Gauss-Markov process with
      correlation time τ and steady-state spread σ = B / GM_ALLAN_PEAK, so
      that its Allan deviation peaks at the datasheet bias instability B.
      Stationary from t = 0.
    - w_a, w_g: white noise, with σ = VRW/√tau_i or ARW/√tau_i per sample.

    The gyro and accelerometer triads draw from separate random streams
    spawned from `rng`, so changing one triad's parameters leaves the
    other's error realization unchanged.

    Args:
        truth: Truth trajectory exposing `t`, `tau_i`, `omega_ib_b`
            (shape (M, 3) [rad/s]) and `f_ib_b` (shape (M, 3) [m/s²]).
        spec: IMU error-parameter set.
        rng: Seeded NumPy random generator. Two child streams are spawned
            from it, one per sensor triad.

    Returns:
        IMUSamples: (meas_omega_ib_b, meas_f_ib_b), the noisy gyro and
            accelerometer outputs, each shape (M, 3).

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from ins_sim.sensors.imu import IMUSpec, generate_imu_samples
        >>> from ins_sim.trajectory.kinematics import TruthTrajectory
        >>> from ins_sim.trajectory.spline import NEDSplinePath
        >>> path = NEDSplinePath([[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [1000.0, 0.0, 0.0]])
        >>> truth = TruthTrajectory.from_spline(path, speed=100.0, tau_i=0.1)
        >>> imu = generate_imu_samples(truth, IMUSpec(), np.random.default_rng(1))
        >>> imu.meas_omega_ib_b.shape == truth.omega_ib_b.shape
        True
    """
    tau_i = truth.tau_i
    rng_gyro, rng_accel = rng.spawn(2)
    meas_omega_ib_b = _triad_measurement(
        rng_gyro, truth.omega_ib_b, tau_i, spec.gyro_sf_std, spec.gyro_ma_std,
        spec.gyro_br_std, spec.gyro_gm_std, spec.gyro_bias_tau, spec.gyro_arw)
    meas_f_ib_b = _triad_measurement(
        rng_accel, truth.f_ib_b, tau_i, spec.accel_sf_std, spec.accel_ma_std,
        spec.accel_br_std, spec.accel_gm_std, spec.accel_bias_tau, spec.accel_vrw)
    return IMUSamples(meas_omega_ib_b, meas_f_ib_b)

docs.title: ins_sim.trajectory.kinematics
docs.text:
Truth trajectory: the reference motion, and what a perfect IMU measures along it.

build_trajectory builds a TruthTrajectory from a mission YAML, phase by phase; TruthTrajectory.from_spline builds one by flying a spline path at constant speed. Either way the truth carries the curvilinear position, velocity and attitude at every sample, plus the outputs a perfect gyro (omega_ib_b) and accelerometer (f_ib_b) would produce.

Those IMU outputs are derived as the exact inverse of the strapdown mechanization's update, so feeding them back through the navigator reproduces the truth to numerical precision. That zero-noise round trip checks the consistency of the two halves; it does not measure how accurately the mechanization integrates continuous motion.

TruthTrajectory(pos_profile: ndarray, v_eb_n: ndarray, euler_nb: ndarray, tau_i: float, L_b0_deg: float = 38.97, lambda_b0_deg: float = -76.49, h_b0: float = 100.0)

Truth state derived from a raw kinematic profile, consistent with rotating-Earth navigation kinematics.

Computed at every sample (Groves notation):

  • Position relative to the start point, r_lb^l (linearized geodetic reprojection, so it is directly comparable to the strapdown output).
  • Velocity v_eb^n (input) and its time derivative (numerical).
  • Curvilinear position (L_b, lambda_b, h_b), integrated from the start.
  • Euler angles (input).
  • Angular rate omega_ib^b that a perfect gyro would output. This includes Earth rate and transport rate, resolved in body axes, via the exact discrete body-to-NED rotation.
  • Specific force f_ib^b that a perfect accelerometer would output, derived from the forward-difference rotating-frame velocity equation so that a forward-Euler strapdown recovers the truth exactly.

Attributes:

    Sample interval [s].

  • t (ndarray) –

    Time vector, shape (M,) [s].

  • r_lb_l (ndarray) –

    Position relative to the start point, resolved in the start point's NED axes, shape (M, 3) [m].

  • v_eb_n (ndarray) –

    Velocity of the body relative to the Earth, resolved in NED, shape (M, 3) [m/s].

  • v_eb_n_dot (ndarray) –

    Time derivative of v_eb_n (central differences, diagnostic only), shape (M, 3) [m/s²].

    Longitude, shape (M,) [rad].

  • h_b (ndarray) –

    Geodetic height, shape (M,) [m].

  • euler_nb (ndarray) –

    Euler angles [phi_nb (roll), theta_nb (pitch), psi_nb (heading)], shape (M, 3) [rad].

  • C_b_n (Rotation) –

    Body-to-NED attitude C_b^n, vectorized over all M samples.

  • omega_ib_b (ndarray) –

    Truth gyro output omega_ib^b, shape (M, 3) [rad/s].

  • f_ib_b (ndarray) –

Builds the truth trajectory from raw position/velocity/Euler-angle profiles.

Parameters:

    Raw NED position profile, shape (M, 3) [m]. Only used to determine the sample count; the exposed r_lb_l attribute is recomputed from the integrated curvilinear position (see class docstring).

  • v_eb_n (ndarray) –

    Velocity profile resolved in NED, shape (M, 3) [m/s].

  • euler_nb (ndarray) –

    Euler angles [roll, pitch, heading], shape (M, 3) [rad].

    Sample interval [s].

    Initial geodetic latitude [deg]. Defaults to 38.97.

  • lambda_b0_deg (float, default: -76.49 ) –

    Initial geodetic height [m]. Defaults to 100.0.

def __init__(self, pos_profile: np.ndarray, v_eb_n: np.ndarray,
             euler_nb: np.ndarray, tau_i: float,
             L_b0_deg: float = 38.97, lambda_b0_deg: float = -76.49,
             h_b0: float = 100.0):
    """Builds the truth trajectory from raw position/velocity/Euler-angle profiles.

    Args:
        pos_profile: Raw NED position profile, shape (M, 3) [m]. Only
            used to determine the sample count; the exposed `r_lb_l`
            attribute is recomputed from the integrated curvilinear
            position (see class docstring).
        v_eb_n: Velocity profile resolved in NED, shape (M, 3) [m/s].
        euler_nb: Euler angles [roll, pitch, heading], shape (M, 3)
            [rad].
        tau_i: Sample interval [s].
        L_b0_deg: Initial geodetic latitude [deg]. Defaults to 38.97.
        lambda_b0_deg: Initial longitude [deg]. Defaults to -76.49.
        h_b0: Initial geodetic height [m]. Defaults to 100.0.
    """
    self.tau_i = tau_i
    L_b0 = np.deg2rad(L_b0_deg)
    lambda_b0 = np.deg2rad(lambda_b0_deg)

    M = len(pos_profile)
    self.t = np.arange(M) * tau_i
    self.v_eb_n = v_eb_n
    self.v_eb_n_dot = np.gradient(v_eb_n, tau_i, axis=0)
    self.euler_nb = euler_nb

    # ---- Curvilinear position by integration --------------------------
    # Integrate (L_b, lambda_b, h_b) using current radii of curvature.
    # Inherently sequential (L_b[k+1] depends on L_b[k]), so this stays
    # a loop.
    # --8<-- [start:truth_position]
    L_b = np.zeros(M); lambda_b = np.zeros(M); h_b = np.zeros(M)
    L_b[0], lambda_b[0], h_b[0] = L_b0, lambda_b0, h_b0
    for k in range(M - 1):
        R_N, R_E = wgs84_radii(L_b[k])
        L_b[k+1] = L_b[k] + (v_eb_n[k, 0] / (R_N + h_b[k])) * tau_i
        lambda_b[k+1] = lambda_b[k] + (v_eb_n[k, 1] /
                                       ((R_E + h_b[k]) * np.cos(L_b[k]))) * tau_i
        h_b[k+1] = h_b[k] - v_eb_n[k, 2] * tau_i
    # --8<-- [end:truth_position]
    self.L_b, self.lambda_b, self.h_b = L_b, lambda_b, h_b

    # Body-to-NED attitude as a vectorized scipy Rotation stack
    self.C_b_n = Rot.from_euler(
        'ZYX', np.column_stack([euler_nb[:, 2], euler_nb[:, 1], euler_nb[:, 0]]))
    C_n_b = self.C_b_n.inv()

    # ---- Truth IMU outputs (exact discrete, vectorized) --------------
    # Consistent with strapdown_navgrade's forward-Euler recursion:
    #   omega_ib_b[k] = exact discrete rotation vector C[k]→C[k+1] / tau_i
    #                   plus Earth/transport rate in body axes
    #   f_ib_b[k]     = forward-difference specific force in NED,
    #                   rotated to body axes:
    #                     f_ib_n[k] = (v[k+1]-v[k])/tau_i + Coriolis[k] - g[k]
    omega_ie_n = earth_rate_n(L_b)                       # (M, 3)
    omega_en_n = transport_rate_n(v_eb_n, L_b, h_b)      # (M, 3)
    g = normal_gravity(L_b, h_b)                         # (M,)
    self.g = g
    g_b_n = np.zeros((M, 3)); g_b_n[:, 2] = g

    # --8<-- [start:truth_specific_force]
    v_eb_n_rate = np.empty((M, 3))
    v_eb_n_rate[:-1] = (v_eb_n[1:] - v_eb_n[:-1]) / tau_i
    v_eb_n_rate[-1]  = v_eb_n_rate[-2]
    f_ib_n = v_eb_n_rate + np.cross(2.0 * omega_ie_n + omega_en_n, v_eb_n) - g_b_n
    self.f_ib_b = C_n_b.apply(f_ib_n)
    # --8<-- [end:truth_specific_force]

    # --8<-- [start:truth_angular_rate]
    dC_b = self.C_b_n[:-1].inv() * self.C_b_n[1:]       # C_b(k+1)^b(k)
    omega_nb_b_fwd = dC_b.as_rotvec() / tau_i            # (M-1, 3)
    omega_nb_b = np.vstack([omega_nb_b_fwd, omega_nb_b_fwd[-1:]])
    self.omega_ib_b = omega_nb_b + C_n_b.apply(omega_ie_n + omega_en_n)
    # --8<-- [end:truth_angular_rate]

    # Reproject truth position through the same linearized geodetic
    # formula that strapdown_navgrade uses, so error =
    # estimated r_lb_l - truth.r_lb_l measures actual navigation error
    # rather than flat-earth vs. curved-earth bias.
    R_N0, R_E0 = wgs84_radii(L_b0)
    r_lb_l = np.zeros((M, 3))
    r_lb_l[:, 0] = (L_b - L_b0)   * (R_N0 + h_b0)
    r_lb_l[:, 1] = (lambda_b - lambda_b[0]) * (R_E0 + h_b0) * np.cos(L_b0)
    r_lb_l[:, 2] = -(h_b - h_b0)
    self.r_lb_l = r_lb_l

Parameters:

    Sample interval [s].

    Truth trajectory over the spline.

Examples:

A 5 km leg flown due north at 100 m/s:

>>> from ins_sim.trajectory.kinematics import TruthTrajectory
>>> from ins_sim.trajectory.spline import NEDSplinePath
>>> path = NEDSplinePath([[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [5000.0, 0.0, 0.0]])
>>> truth = TruthTrajectory.from_spline(path, speed=100.0, tau_i=0.1)
>>> [round(float(v), 6) for v in truth.v_eb_n[100]]
[100.0, 0.0, 0.0]
Source code in ins_sim/trajectory/kinematics.py 
@classmethod
def from_spline(cls, path: NEDSplinePath, speed: float, tau_i: float,
                 L_b0_deg: float = 38.97, lambda_b0_deg: float = -76.49,
                 h_b0: float = 100.0) -> "TruthTrajectory":
    """Builds a truth trajectory by traversing a spline path at constant speed.

    Args:
        path: NED spline path to traverse.
        speed: Along-path speed [m/s], assumed constant.
        tau_i: Sample interval [s].
        L_b0_deg: Initial geodetic latitude [deg]. Defaults to 38.97.
        lambda_b0_deg: Initial longitude [deg]. Defaults to -76.49.
        h_b0: Initial geodetic height [m]. Defaults to 100.0.

    Returns:
        TruthTrajectory: Truth trajectory over the spline.

    Examples:
        A 5 km leg flown due north at 100 m/s:

        >>> from ins_sim.trajectory.kinematics import TruthTrajectory
        >>> from ins_sim.trajectory.spline import NEDSplinePath
        >>> path = NEDSplinePath([[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [5000.0, 0.0, 0.0]])
        >>> truth = TruthTrajectory.from_spline(path, speed=100.0, tau_i=0.1)
        >>> [round(float(v), 6) for v in truth.v_eb_n[100]]
        [100.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    """
    T = path.length / speed
    t = np.arange(0.0, T + tau_i, tau_i)
    s_of_t = np.minimum(speed * t, path.length)
    pos_profile = path.position(s_of_t)
    v_eb_n = np.gradient(pos_profile, tau_i, axis=0)
    # Coordinated-turn bank uses local gravity at the start; for short
    # trajectories using a mean g is well within the rounding error
    # of the heading-rate derivative itself.
    g_ref = normal_gravity(np.deg2rad(L_b0_deg), h_b0)
    euler_nb = _euler_from_velocity(v_eb_n, tau_i, g_ref)
    return cls(pos_profile, v_eb_n, euler_nb, tau_i,
               L_b0_deg=L_b0_deg, lambda_b0_deg=lambda_b0_deg, h_b0=h_b0)

Builds a phase-by-phase truth trajectory from a YAML mission definition.

Each phase in the YAML maps to a helper function; fields omitted from a phase are inherited from the running state (heading, speed, altitude).

Parameters:

  • yaml_path (str) –

    Path to the YAML mission-phase definition file.

  • tau_i (float | None, default: None ) –

Raises:
